newsitem.title: USA: IMF staff supports Argentina's revised program.
newsitem.headline: IMF staff supports Argentina's revised program.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund's management said Friday it supported the basic elements of Argentina's new economic program.

"(The revised program) includes important measures in the structural reform area that will help to strengthen the ongoing recovery of econmic activity and employment", the IMF said in a news release quoting its managing director, Michel Camdessus.
It added that Camdessus was prepared to recommend the new Argentine program when the IMF's executive board reviews it in October.
Argentina's new economy minister, Roque Fernndez, last month drafted a package of austerity measures that included tax increases designed to close a yawning budget deficit.
He also negotiated new economic targets with the IMF, which in April granted Argentina a $1.05 billion standby loan.
The IMF's press release said it expected to receive soon a letter from Argentine authorities outlining the economic reforms.

Fernndez has said in Buenos Aires that the IMF would allow the Argentine government to post a $5.0 billion budget deficit this year, instead of the $2.5 billion agreed by his predecessor, Domingo Cavallo.
The shortfall would have to decrease to $3.0 billion in 1997, when Argentina will seek an extended fund facility program with the IMF.
Fernndez has argued that the revenue gap could balloon to $6.6 billion this year if tax revenue is not boosted.
The Argentine Senate has approved part of his tax package but the lower house of Congress has yet to vote on it.
